market_context: United States; composition of plain raw or roasted peanuts without coatings.
title: Peanuts: Protein, Fat, Fiber, and Calories

seo.title: Peanuts: Protein, Fat, Fiber, and Calories
seo.meta_description: Per 100 g, peanuts provide about 26 g protein, 49 g fat, and 8–9 g fiber. A 1-ounce serving is roughly 160–170 calories and 7 g protein.
seo.search_intent: Understand peanut nutrition and translate per-100-g numbers into a realistic serving.

excerpt: Peanuts are energy-dense, but they are also high in protein and mostly unsaturated fat. Per 100 g they contain roughly 26 g protein, 49 g fat, and 8–9 g fiber. A 1-ounce serving provides about 160–170 calories, 7 g protein, 14 g fat, and 2–3 g fiber.
content_html:
Botanically, peanuts are legumes, even though nutritionally and culturally they are usually grouped with nuts. Their defining combination is high energy density plus a substantial amount of protein.

What 100 g and one ounce provide

NutrientApprox./100 gApprox./28 g
Calories~567~160
Protein~26 g~7.3 g
Fat~49 g~13.7 g
Fiber~8.5 g~2.4 g

Numbers vary slightly between raw, dry-roasted, oil-roasted, salted, and coated products.

Most of the fat is unsaturated

Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids make up most of peanut fat. That does not erase calories: fat provides about 9 calories per gram, so a small handful carries substantial energy.

Protein is high compared with many nuts

At around 26 g per 100 g, peanuts tend to exceed almonds, walnuts, and cashews in protein. A realistic one-ounce portion still delivers about 7 g.

A serving tells a different story from 100 grams

One hundred grams is useful for comparing foods, but it is much more than a typical serving of peanuts. At roughly 30 g, calories and fat fall to about 30% of the table values while still providing meaningful protein and fiber. That translation explains how peanuts can be nutrient-rich and energy-dense at the same time.

It also prevents a tablespoon of peanut butter, a handful of peanuts and 100 g from being treated as equivalent intakes. The food and the amount both matter.

Processing changes the product

Plain dry-roasted peanuts differ from honey-roasted, candy-coated, or heavily salted versions. Added oil, sugar, and sodium can substantially change the nutritional profile.

Peanuts are nutrient-dense in both meanings of the word: they pack protein, fat, fiber, and calories into a small serving.

faq.question: How much protein is in peanuts?
faq.answer: About 26 g per 100 g, or roughly 7 g in a 1-ounce serving.

faq.question: Are peanuts high in fat?
faq.answer: Yes, around 49 g per 100 g, with most of the fat unsaturated.

faq.question: Are peanuts nuts or legumes?
faq.answer: Botanically they are legumes, but nutritionally and culinarily they are commonly grouped with nuts.
